data.body:
caused_by established — the cause site IS the fix site (date test applied).

`git log -S 'subprocess.Popen' -- src/rebar/llm/workflow/snapshot.py` returns exactly one
commit: 9f1e92c659 (2026-06-18, "feat(workflow): WS-D2 — hardened git-ref filesystem
snapshot"), the commit that created the file. The unbounded Popen, the undrained
`stderr=PIPE`, and the inherited stdin were all present from the first line of the file;
no later edit introduced or aggravated them (the only subsequent touches are
7622149b15/06e5992644/fc792e4f3c/997ecaabbf/a9aed66ce4 — prior-art hardening, ruff style,
the portable rename-then-chmod publish, and the BLE001/RUF ratchets).

Date test against the obligations that WOULD have caught it — every one of them POSTDATES
the cause commit, so this is NOT an unmet obligation of any of them:

  * 747f (blobless fetch, `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300`)   — 2026-07-31
  * 77e1 (bound remaining network git calls)      — 2026-07-31
  * 12e4 (throughput-keyed stall abort)           — 2026-08-02
  * d37e (`check_raw_git_writes.py` marker gate)  — 2026-08-03
  * cause commit 9f1e92c659                       — 2026-06-18

The one precedent that predates it is c16f (5752edaefe, 2026-06-15, "bound network git
subprocesses with a timeout" on `_store/push.py`), three days earlier — but c16f scoped
itself to NETWORK git subprocesses, and `git archive` on a local repo only reaches the
network through the non-obvious promisor lazy-fetch path. Calling this an unmet c16f
obligation would be a stretch; the honest attribution is that WS-D2 (`humid-hub-sword`,
cf7c-1832-d5cd-4aa3) introduced the defect in the code it wrote. Linked caused_by.

Noting for completeness that 77e1's own commit message claims to "close the rest of the
class in the two modules that were still unbounded" (gerrit_client, opcert workspace) —
it missed this site because `git archive` was not classified as network-capable. That is a
classification gap in a sweep, not the origin of the defect.
